images.alt: Biscayne National Park

images.caption:
Snorkelers
Ninety-five percent of Biscayne National Park's 173,000 acres are covered by water, making it the largest marine park in the National Park System. Four major ecosystems are protected within the park. They are: 
- a narrow fringe of mangrove forest along the mainland shoreline of Biscayne Bay; 
- the clear shallow waters of Biscayne Bay itself; 
- the northernmost islands of the Florida Keys; and 
- the beginning of the world's third-longest coral reef tract. 
This mix of upland and marine environments provides habitat for hundreds of species of animals and plants.
Keywords: bisc; National parks and reserves; Coral reefs; Recreational activities; Fishing

images.filename: Marine Debris Display- Biscayne National Park (89c8cfac-ee82-4085-9932-6845b3507f91).jpg
images.caption:
a man in national park service uniform sits on a bench inside a circular acrylic sculpture with marine debris encased inside. The top of the sculpture says "Biscayne National Park" and next to the sculpture is a wayside.
The marine debris display at Biscayne National Park is located in the Dante Fascell Visitor Center. The display features an acrylic sculpture with marine debris encased inside and a bench to sit in the middle of the ring - the perfect place to snap a photo and share on social media to spread awareness. The exhibit also features a bi-lingual wayside.
Keywords: marine debris
